clue.text: Lines husband may like but with no margins

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its outside letters, its margins, leaving only the inner part

explanation.surface: A wife's comment that her husband might enjoy something, provided it has no margins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no margins' strips the ends from may, like and but, leaving A, IK and U.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese poem of seventeen syllables is a few short lines of verse.

clue.text: Ambitious person's gamey promotional leaflet

parts.note: game meat that is gamey is described as high, slightly off
a flyer is a handbill advertising something

explanation.surface: An ambitious marketer's leaflet smells of game.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aiming for great success, a go-getter, is described this way.

clue.text: Pulley that moves sideways, but not at first

indicators.note: not at first drops the first letter of the word found

parts.note: one who sidles moves sideways furtively, a sidler

explanation.surface: A description of a pulley wheel that shifts sideways, though not initially.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering a free-running guide wheel on a belt drive is called an idler pulley.

clue.text: Joined place of higher learning following international education

parts.note: uni is short for university
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone joined a university after an international schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Things brought together into one whole are united, merged or joined.

clue.text: Overwhelmed operator requisitioned

parts.note: pressed, as in pressed into service, means commandeered

explanation.surface: A worker swamped after being drafted in by the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: Being crushed or weighed down by hardship is a synonym for feeling overwhelmed.

clue.text: Funny when Jack leaves mince pie

indicators.note: leaves says the letter for jack departs from the word

parts.note: jocular means joking, funny
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A joke about a sailor leaving behind his Christmas mince pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince pie' is Cockney rhyming slang for eye; the answer is the adjective, used here as a noun for an eyepiece or eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang turns eye into mince pie, and the answer means relating to the eye.

clue.text: Maintain pressure with troops available in emergency

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
the reserve is the body of troops held back for emergencies

explanation.surface: Keeping up the pressure with soldiers held back for a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something in its existing state is to keep it going, a synonym for maintain.

clue.text: Nonsense served up supporting almost adequate notional line

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits underneath, so it comes after
almost means the last letter is dropped from the word found

parts.note: equal, as in equal to the task, means adequate

indicators.note: served up, in a down clue, means the word is brought upwards, read bottom to top

parts.note: rot means rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: Rubbish is dished up alongside a barely satisfactory idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns ROT into TOR; 'almost' clips EQUAL to EQUA, and TOR goes below it.
explanation.definitionFit: The great circle around the Earth's middle is an imaginary, notional line.

clue.text: Romanians reconstructed small republic

indicators.note: reconstructed means rebuilt in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Romanians rebuilt a little republic.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny state enclosed by Italy is one of the world's smallest republics.

clue.text: Remained in good health mostly in empty desert

indicators.note: the shortened health word goes inside the hollowed desert
empty means the word desert is hollowed out, keeping just its ends
mostly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to be well is to be in good health

explanation.surface: A traveller stayed healthy, more or less, in a bare desert.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lived or stayed somewhere is to have resided, a synonym of remained.

clue.text: Aquatic bird, funny-looking alien gull

indicators.note: something funny-looking is oddly shaped, so these letters are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a strange gull that looks like an alien.
explanation.definitionFit: The moorhen family includes this water bird, a marsh-dwelling rail.

clue.text: Parts of chicken wings perhaps rejected in epicurean lunch

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gourmet sends back the chicken wings served at lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: These forearm bones appear in birds' wings too, so a chicken wing contains them, as an example.

clue.text: Plastic laminate having as function glass replacement?

parts.note: what a thing is for is its function, as in 'a knife is for cutting'
mica, in thin sheets, was used instead of glass in stove and lantern windows

explanation.surface: A plastic surface being put to use in place of glass.
explanation.definitionFit: This trademarked heat-resistant sheet is a well-known kitchen worktop material.

clue.text: Person taking part in hospital department harangue

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
to rant is to harangue loudly

explanation.surface: A participant in a hospital department launches into a tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone entered in a competition is a participant in it.

clue.text: Year with disastrous slide in outputs

indicators.note: a disastrous slide is a collapse, so the word's letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An economic report on a year when a disastrous slide hit production.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm's or investment's returns are what it produces, so outputs.

clue.text: Archaeopteryx maybe was one that caught nematodes?

definitions.meaning: archaeopteryx is one of the first known birds, an example of a primitive flier
the proverb says this one catches the worm, and nematodes are worms

explanation.surface: A palaeontologist wonders whether a fossil bird fed on roundworms.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt riser is called this after the proverb about catching the worm, and archaeopteryx was literally an ancient one.

clue.text: General survey done — into German car, that is

parts.note: over means finished, done

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is goes into the middle of the car make

parts.note: VW is Volkswagen, the German car maker
IE is id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A survey of the German car market is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad summary of a subject is a general survey of it.

clue.text: Fat whiner given facelift might become so very slim

indicators.note: a facelift remodels a face, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A plump complainer hopes cosmetic surgery will make them skinny.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as thin as a wafer is extremely slender, so very slim.

clue.text: What's over one's head? Hat's upside down in Yorkshire river!

indicators.note: the inverted headgear goes inside the river

parts.note: the Aire is a river flowing through Leeds in Yorkshire

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: hat is a cap, so hat's gives caps

explanation.surface: Someone's hat has ended up floating upside down in a Yorkshire river.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: the sky above you is the space over your head.
explanation.definitionFit: The sky above a territory, controlled by its state, is literally what lies over your head.

clue.text: Something exceptional in skirt topless divas modelled

parts.note: a ra-ra skirt is a short frilled skirt worn by cheerleaders

indicators.note: modelled means shaped anew, so the remaining letters are rearranged
topless takes the head letter off the word divas

explanation.surface: Divas pose topless while modelling skirts on a catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes D from divas, leaving IVAS, and 'modelled' rearranges that to AVIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means a rare bird, used of an unusual or exceptional person or thing.

clue.text: Film Chemical Engineer introduced into a gallery

indicators.note: the engineer's letters are put inside the gallery phrase

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
CE stands for chemical engineer (also civil engineer)

explanation.surface: A chemical engineer is brought into an art gallery for a film showing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellulose-based plastic sheet was the base of photographic film, so it names film.

clue.text: Disconcert upper-class swell turning up first

indicators.note: first puts the flipped word ahead of the swell
turning means the little word up is flipped round

parts.note: a toff is a posh, upper-class person, a swell

explanation.surface: A posh gentleman is rattled when somebody shows up ahead of him.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone off is to distract or unsettle them, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Releases peacekeepers with army unit — a thousand for power

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are United Nations troops

indicators.note: for means one letter takes the place of the other

parts.note: a corps is a large army unit
P is the physics symbol for power
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers join an army unit while a thousand are swapped for the powerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling the stopper from bottles lets their contents out, releasing them; figuratively it means letting loose.

clue.text: Young royal repeated expression of disapproval

indicators.note: repeated says the young king's name is given twice over

parts.note: Tut, Tutankhamun, was the boy king of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: A young prince keeps saying something disapproving.
explanation.definitionFit: A clicking sound of the tongue is the conventional exclamation of disapproval.

clue.text: Evasive behaviour of company head about yen

indicators.note: the company and headland pair sit around the currency letter

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Fife Ness
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: The firm's boss is cagey about questions on Japanese currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Shy reluctance to commit or reveal oneself is behaviour that is evasive.

clue.text: Native American large lobster trap

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A Native American sets a big trap for lobsters.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicker basket for catching or carrying fish and shellfish, used as a pot.

clue.text: Expose extremely uncommon pretext

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters, the two ends of the word uncommon

parts.note: a cover is a front or pretext concealing a real purpose

explanation.surface: Unmasking a remarkably rare excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal or lay bare something hidden is to expose it.

clue.text: Food from Italy in vehicle before start of delivery

indicators.note: before puts the van piece ahead of the next letter
the letter for Italy sits inside the vehicle

parts.note: a van is a delivery vehicle
I is the international vehicle registration letter for Italy

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of delivery

explanation.surface: Food from Italy is loaded into a van before the delivery begins.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or literary word for an item of food, a victual.

clue.text: A glazed fabric put round plant

indicators.note: put round means turned the other way, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: ciré is a fabric with a glazed, shiny finish

explanation.surface: Shiny fabric is wrapped around a pot plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather belongs to this genus, so the name is a plant.

clue.text: A fine time at hotel? There's consequences!

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a term is a period of time, as in a school term
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A pleasant stay at a hotel, followed by a warning of what comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: The period of results that follows an event is its outcome or consequences.

clue.text: Doddery old chaps going in to get accommodation

indicators.note: doddery means shaky and unsteady, so the word old wobbles into a new order
the men go inside the word get

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: Shaky old men going inside to find a room for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A place to lodge or stay is a form of lodging, so accommodation.

clue.text: Litter of unlimited beds in convalescent home

indicators.note: the core of beds goes inside the short word for sanatorium

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a home for convalescents

indicators.note: unlimited strips the word beds of its boundary letters

explanation.surface: A care home with endless beds full of litter.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter is a carried chair, and a sedan chair is that kind of conveyance.
